scope: Four independent million-row functional/recovery cases; exact body/receipt/history reconciliation executed inside each case before successful cleanup. Short phases are not sustained comparative performance. Old 10000-row checkpoint remains in MUTABLE_RESULTS.json. The final sustained publisher independently replays these prerequisite proofs again.

backend_contract.atomicity: Each two-row change and its receipt are one synchronous database transaction. Group count, amount sum and payload length stay fixed, while stored bodies and revisions genuinely change.
backend_contract.durability: Every connection sets/checks CedarDB async_commit=off or PostgreSQL synchronous_commit=on, fsync=on, full_page_writes=on. Retained-volume process/container crash is distinct from device/power loss.
backend_contract.retries: No mutation replay. All submitted errors remain ambiguous until native receipts and complete bodies are reconciled with fsynced external intents. Later requests use new sequence IDs.
backend_contract.deletes: Two rows are deleted and reinserted inside one transaction; readers must never see the transient missing pair. Permanent delete/TTL/reclamation workloads remain separate.

backend_contract.limits: Single Docker VM, no HA/replica/sharding claim. Same-key multi-writer conflicts, arbitrary update effects, permanent deletes, verified OS-cold access, open-loop saturation, disk EIO/full and physical power-loss recovery are unqualified. backend_contract.atomicity: Each two-row change and its receipt are one synchronous database transaction. Group count, amount sum and payload length stay fixed, while stored bodies and revisions genuinely change.
backend_contract.durability: Every connection sets/checks CedarDB async_commit=off or PostgreSQL synchronous_commit=on, fsync=on, full_page_writes=on. Retained-volume process/container crash is distinct from device/power loss.
backend_contract.retries: No mutation replay. All submitted errors remain ambiguous until native receipts and complete bodies are reconciled with fsynced external intents. Later requests use new sequence IDs.
backend_contract.deletes: Two rows are deleted and reinserted inside one transaction; readers must never see the transient missing pair. Permanent delete/TTL/reclamation workloads remain separate.

client.arrival: ticker-paced closed loop; missed ticks under backpressure are not queued
client.tls: disabled on the isolated lab network

data.types: BIGINT PK id; INTEGER customer/amount; TEXT payload; BIGINT revision
data.pattern: Each selected pair receives UPDATE then DELETE/reinsert; cycle through the configured pair window. Same analytical bucket, balanced signed amount adjustment, same payload length. One final pair remains historical and immutable.
data.payload: 192 bytes of repeated customer prefix plus 64 ASCII SHA256 hex characters; versioned suffix for actual mutations

backend_contract.oracle: Native receipt set must include every ACK and only externally intended sequences. Replay committed sequences, then verify every seeded row/version/body and all 100 group invariants. Independent snapshots verify latest committed pair and an older untouched pair; UTC prior-ACK watermark check uses a documented 10ms guard.
backend_contract.namespace: New UUID schema per case; preserve failed schemas. Drop a successful schema only after actors stop and complete external exports are fsynced/verified. Base orders fixture remains unchanged and independently verified.
backend_contract.resources: One active backend per performance cell, 4 CPUs/6 GiB/no swap. Each Go actor has 1 CPU/512 MiB/no swap; 1 analytical actor alone or 3 actors with mutations. Whole-store counters include the retained immutable base fixture as well as mutable data, receipts, indexes, WAL and engine files.
backend_contract.limits: Single Docker VM, no HA/replica/sharding claim. Same-key multi-writer conflicts, arbitrary update effects, permanent deletes, verified OS-cold access, open-loop saturation, disk EIO/full and physical power-loss recovery are unqualified. CedarDB engine source is closed; inspect versioned public APIs, shipped configuration and pinned pgx/PostgreSQL source.

config.contract: Synchronous repeatable-read transactions. Each paired UPDATE or DELETE/reinsert and its native receipt commit atomically. External intent/ACK journal; no mutation retries. Whole group totals stay fixed while actual queried bodies change.

read_history.scope: Four-body repeatable-read snapshots and prior-ACK watermark lower bounds; shared-VM UTC with a conservative guard, not a general linearizability proof

compression.scope: Off-path CSV compressibility, not native engine compression
Off-path CSV compressibility, not native engine compression

postgres.io_scope: Kernel per-device and per-interface counters, with reset intervals excluded. Missing fields are unavailable, not zero. Do not sum stacked devices or both endpoints into physical traffic; raw counters remain authoritative.
postgres.scope: About 1s cadence. CPU covers deltas between usable native samples; restart/reset intervals and initial/final partial intervals are excluded, not estimated. Raw block I/O and all native fields remain in JSONL. This is not process RSS or a complete CPU total across crashes.
